en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
11. The Mansion of the First Faithful Wife “Curlews,
peacocks, and celestial swans,
and cuckoos with melodious voices, fly down together;”
This delightful celestial mansion is strewn with flowers,
variegated and frequented by men and women;
there you dwell, O goddess of great majesty.
They display supernormal powers in many forms;
and these nymphs all around you dance, sing, and bring delight.
O lady of great majesty, you have attained divine power;
while still a human being, what merit did you perform?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing splendor?
"And your complexion shines in all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she explained the deed whose fruit this is:
"When I was among humans, having become human..."
I was devoted and pleasing to others;
like a mother protecting her son,
even when angry, I did not speak harshly.
Established in truth, having abandoned the offense of lying,
they delight in giving, having integrated their being;
with confident hearts, [they give] food and drink.
I gave a vast gift with due respect.
Because of that, such is my complexion;
because of that, it is found here in me.
And riches arise for me,
whatever is dear to the mind.
I declare this to you, O bhikkhu of great power.
"While I was a human being, I performed meritorious deeds;
therefore, I possess such blazing power,
and my radiance illuminates every direction."
The first Vimāna on Faithfulness, the eleventh.
